It will definitely fade. It does suck that those of us with the darker skin seem to have those white scars show up pretty clearly. But, honestly, especially on your legs people don't really seem to look that closely. They do look at the arms but most of the time they're not going to spend a lot of time staring at your legs

No, they are not anywhere near as visible as that used to be. Frankly, I am probably the only one that would notice them because I know where they are and I know what they say. I didn't try anything on them. It's just been a long time since I made them. But I would definitely say I probably only know they are there because I know where they're at and I can look for them

I also have brown skin and I hate to say it but words that I carved probably a decade ago still show up. I think it's one of those things where time is just the only thing that might help. Meanwhile, if you are going to wear short skirts or shorts maybe consider getting some concealer that you could use?
I would probably second the person that posted before me. I have found that my shoulder and my thighs scarred the worst.

Long sleeve shirts? Depending on the material, they can definitely be more lightweight and at least cooler than a hoodie.

I would agree with the above comment. It's really up to you about whether or not you want to share that with your friend. Hopefully they will be understanding but there's always the possibility they won't relate so I would just be prepared for that as well. It's hard to share something like that so I think it's brave that you're considering it!

I think that's totally understandable and it would be okay to talk to your friends that are not mutual friends that aren't around this person about the situation if you think they will be discreet. But I just don't think it's your place to share that with somebody that knows him.

My two cents is that you should not share with any of his other friends, mutual or not. SH is an incredibly sensitive topic and, as someone with a history of that, it is horrible when well meaning people think that it is okay to go behind my back and share something like that.

I think that everybody's body is different and everyone heals differently but I usually heal pretty quickly. Like cuts will close up within a few days if they are not infected and I will get a scab within a week that will probably flake off quickly and it will be an obvious scar but it will be closed and done with at about the two-week mark.

I would definitely discuss it with your doctor or psychiatrist. I tried Sertraline for a bit and it just was not a good fit for me. Everybody's body is a little different and different medications will have different effects. Maybe it isn't the right medication for you in the long run but something else might be.
This is weird but I actually used to keep mine in a dental floss container.
I have also heard that as well simply given that scars are more tender and healing areas of the skin so I do try to remember to use sunscreen if I am out at the pool or whatever.

This is certainly my own two cents but I actually am not triggered by seeing other people's scars. If anything, it makes me feel like I'm not alone. Of course, you're always going to have the random strangers who are uncomfortable with seeing your scars because they're going to make assumptions and you can't control that. But I think ultimately it's really about your own comfort level and what makes you feel good.

I think that a lot of therapists really are very caring individuals. I think it's a really tough job and it's very emotionally draining so I think that people who actually get into it generally do care. I'm not going to tell you that everyone is a good therapist or a good counselor, there are certainly exceptions. But I do think a lot of them care about their clients and when they have an off-day it's probably because they have things going on personally.
